newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian vehicle sales up slightly in 1996.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian vehicle sales up slightly in 1996.

text.p: Australian new vehicle sales rose 1.2 percent in calendar 1996 compared with 1995 but sales are expected to fall three percent in 1997, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries (FCAI) said on Wednesday.

Vehicles sales for 1996 totalled 650,049, an increase of 7,492 over the 1995 year, the industry organisation said in its monthly VFACTS publication. "Forecasting for 1997, at this early stage, suggests a market of 630,000 units at best, some 20,000 or three percent down on 1996," the FCAI said.

"On an international comparison, the Australian new vehicle market should be closer to 700,000 units, or 500,000 passenger cars and 200,000 commercial vehicles," FCAI chief executive Ian Grigg said in a statement. "Without such volumes it is very difficult for Australia to have a modern fleet of safe and environmentally clean vehicles," he said.

The FCAI said the 1996 increase could be attributed to the light truck Market, with a rise of 6,381 vehicles or 4.7 percent, and to a minor rise in the passenger vehicle market of 3,686 vehicles or 0.8 percent.
The heavy truck market fell 14.5 percent or 2,575 vehicles in 1996, FCAI said.
It said the December monthly market totalled 54,215 units, a 2.5 percent increase on December 1995, but down 2.1 percent on November's 55,368.

Among the vehicle manufacturers with plants in Australia, Ford Motor Co kept its market lead in 1996 with sales of 132,205 for a market share of 20.3 percent but this was down from a year earlier when sales were 137,862 (21.5 percent).
General Motors Co was second with sales of 127,367 vehicles for a market share of 19.6 percent, which compared with 1995 sales of 126,473 and a market share of 19.7 percent.
Toyota Motor Co sold 121,209 vehicles for a market share of 18.6 percent. This compared with sales of 121,059 in 1995 and a market share of 18.8 percent for the year.
Mitsubishi Motors Corp, the fourth car manufacturer in Australia, sold 61,079 vehicles in 1996 for a market share of 9.4 percent, down from 65,028 in 1996 and a market share of 10.1 percent.

The rest of the sales were made up by imports, led by Hyundai Motor Co with sales of 48,871 and a market share of 7.5 percent. In 1995 the South Korean car maker sold 34,932 vehicles for a market share of 5.4 percent.
